sentence: Tirzepatide is a prescription medicine used to manage type 2 diabetes and to treat obesity.
note: NHS page title: a medicine to manage type 2 diabetes and treat obesity; NHS: only available with a prescription.

sentence: It activates two gut hormone receptors, GLP-1 and GIP.
note: NHS summary: GLP-1/GIP agonist acting on two gut hormone receptors.

sentence: Feeling or being sick is among the common side effects, inflammation of the pancreas is a serious one, it may reduce how well the contraceptive pill works in people who are overweight, and the NHS says it is not used in pregnancy.
note: Compound of ledgered sentences below (side effects: NHS; pill: MHRA overweight qualifier).

sentence: Managing type 2 diabetes in adults who meet NICE criteria, alongside diet and exercise
note: TA924 recommends for type 2 diabetes alongside diet and exercise, for adults meeting criteria (original text; NICE has proposed an update, final wording not retrieved).

sentence: Treating overweight and obesity in adults, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity as part of a weight management programme
note: TA1026: alongside reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity; NHS: only prescribed alongside programmes supporting diet and activity changes.

sentence: Tirzepatide activates the receptors for two gut hormones, GLP-1 and GIP, so it is called a dual agonist.
note: NHS: GLP-1/GIP agonist, two gut hormone receptors; Kent and Medway: dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist.

sentence: For weight loss, the NHS says it reduces appetite and helps people feel fuller for longer.
note: NHS: for weight loss reduces appetite and helps you feel full for longer.

sentence: For type 2 diabetes, it lowers blood sugar and helps the body make more insulin when needed.
note: NHS: for type 2 diabetes lowers blood sugar and helps the body make more insulin when needed.

sentence: The NHS lists feeling sick and being sick among the common side effects
note: NHS side effects list nausea and vomiting among common effects.

sentence: Constipation, diarrhoea, stomach pain, tiredness, hair loss and redness at the injection site are also listed by the NHS
note: NHS list: constipation, diarrhoea, stomach pain, tiredness, injection-site redness, hair loss.

sentence: Inflamed pancreas (acute pancreatitis), which can cause severe pain in the stomach or back that does not go away, is listed by the NHS
note: NHS: acute pancreatitis, severe pain in stomach or back which does not go away.

sentence: Gallstones or swelling of the gallbladder, which can cause severe tummy pain, are listed by the NHS
note: NHS page: gallstones or gallbladder swelling can cause severe tummy pain (blended summary; attributed to the NHS medicines page by two separate searches).

sentence: Low blood sugar, more likely with other diabetes medicines, can cause headaches, vision problems, feeling dizzy, weak or confused, a fast heartbeat or sweating
note: NHS: low blood sugar, more likely with other diabetes medicines; symptoms headaches, vision problems, dizzy, weak or confused, fast heartbeat, sweating.

sentence: Serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis): swollen throat or tongue, a raised itchy rash or difficulty breathing
note: NHS: anaphylaxis can cause swollen throat or tongue, raised itchy rash or difficulty breathing.

sentence: Severe pain that does not go away needs urgent advice from NHS 111 or the GP; signs of a serious allergic reaction are an emergency that needs a 999 call
note: Site signposting rule (README): 111/GP for urgent, 999 for emergency; retrieved NHS summaries gave no explicit route for this page, so the route is textbook, not attributed to the NHS.

sentence: Tirzepatide is a prescription medicine used to manage type 2 diabetes and to treat obesity.
note: as above

sentence: In the UK it is sold under the brand name Mounjaro.
note: NHS and Cheshire and Merseyside page title 'Mounjaro (Tirzepatide)'.

sentence: It is an injection that people give themselves.
note: NHS-style wording: injection just under the skin which you do yourself; Mounjaro user manual.

sentence: NICE has recommended tirzepatide for some adults with type 2 diabetes who meet set criteria, alongside diet and exercise.
NICE has also recommended it as an option for adults with overweight or obesity, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity.
note: TA1026 1.1: recommended as an option alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

sentence: NICE links this to a person's starting body mass index and to having at least one weight-related health condition.
note: TA1026: initial BMI threshold and at least one weight-related comorbidity (figure omitted deliberately).

sentence: NICE applies a lower body mass index threshold for people from some ethnic backgrounds.
note: TA1026: lower BMI thresholds for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean backgrounds.

sentence: For weight management, the NHS says tirzepatide is only prescribed alongside programmes that support changes to diet and physical activity.
note: NHS: only prescribed alongside programmes supporting weight loss through diet and activity changes.

sentence: Tirzepatide activates the receptors for two gut hormones, GLP-1 and GIP, so it is called a dual agonist.
note: as above

sentence: For weight loss, the NHS says it reduces appetite and helps people feel fuller for longer.
note: as above

sentence: For type 2 diabetes, it lowers blood sugar and helps the body make more insulin when needed.
note: as above

sentence: An NHS medicines optimisation newsletter adds that it increases insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon release and slows the emptying of the stomach.
note: Kent and Medway newsletter: increases insulin sensitivity and secretion, suppresses glucagon secretion, slows gastric emptying.

sentence: NICE says it can be used in primary care or in specialist weight management services.
note: TA1026: can be used in primary care or specialist weight management services.

sentence: Access on the NHS in England is being phased in, so not everyone who fits the NICE recommendation can have it at once.
note: TA1026 funding variation: not everyone can have it in the first years; highest clinical need first.

sentence: NHS England's interim commissioning guidance sets out which groups are offered it first.
note: NHS England interim commissioning guidance sets eligible cohorts and phased implementation.

sentence: The NHS lists feeling sick and being sick among the common side effects.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: It also lists constipation, diarrhoea, stomach pain, tiredness, hair loss and redness at the injection site.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: The NHS says most serious side effects are rare.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: The NHS lists inflammation of the pancreas (acute pancreatitis), which can cause severe pain in the stomach or back that does not go away, as a serious side effect.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: The NHS also lists gallstones or swelling of the gallbladder, which can cause severe tummy pain.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: A serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) can cause a swollen throat or tongue, a raised itchy rash or difficulty breathing.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: The NHS lists low blood sugar, which is more likely when tirzepatide is used with other diabetes medicines and can cause headaches, vision problems, feeling dizzy, weak or confused, a fast heartbeat or sweating.
note: NHS medicines page (see sideEffects rows).

sentence: Severe pain that does not go away needs urgent advice from NHS 111 or the GP, and signs of a serious allergic reaction are an emergency that needs a 999 call.
note: Site signposting rule; not attributed to the NHS.

sentence: A South West London NHS information sheet for prescribers warns that sickness and diarrhoea can lead to dehydration, which could worsen kidney function.
note: SW London ICB information sheet: nausea/vomiting/diarrhoea may lead to dehydration and deterioration in renal function.

sentence: The MHRA says GLP-1 medicines may reduce how well oral contraceptives work in people who are overweight or obese.
note: GOV.UK guidance: GLP-1 medicines may reduce effectiveness of oral contraceptives in those who are overweight or obese.

sentence: For people who are overweight and taking Mounjaro, the MHRA advises using a non-oral method of contraception in addition to the pill.
note: MHRA statement: patients who are overweight and taking Mounjaro are advised to use a non-oral form of contraception in addition to the pill.

sentence: The MHRA lists the pill and non-oral methods such as the implant, coil or condoms as effective contraception.
note: MHRA guidance: effective contraception includes the pill and non-oral methods such as the implant, coil or condoms.

sentence: The NHS says it is best to avoid alcohol, because alcohol can increase side effects such as feeling or being sick.
note: NHS: best to avoid alcohol as it can increase side effects like feeling or being sick.

sentence: Low blood sugar is more likely when tirzepatide is combined with other diabetes medicines.
note: NHS.

sentence: The NHS says most adults can use tirzepatide.
note: NHS.

sentence: It may not suit people who have had an allergic reaction to tirzepatide or a similar GLP-1 medicine, or who have had acute pancreatitis.
note: NHS: may not suit people who had allergic reaction to tirzepatide or another GLP-1 agonist or who have had acute pancreatitis.

sentence: The NHS says tirzepatide is not used in pregnancy because there is not enough information about its effects on a baby.
note: NHS: not used in pregnancy, not enough information.

sentence: The MHRA says GLP-1 medicines should not be taken during pregnancy, while trying to get pregnant or during breastfeeding, because of a lack of human data.
note: MHRA: should not be taken during pregnancy, while trying to get pregnant, or during breastfeeding; lack of human safety data.

sentence: The MHRA also advises that people who could become pregnant take steps to avoid pregnancy while using GLP-1 medicines.
note: MHRA: patients who may become pregnant should take steps to avoid pregnancy.

sentence: The NHS says it is not known whether tirzepatide passes into breast milk.
note: NHS: not known if the medicine passes into breast milk.

sentence: NICE says that if too little of the starting weight has been lost after six months at the highest tolerated dose, the prescriber decides whether to continue, weighing the benefits and risks for that person.
note: TA1026 clinician guidance: less than 5% initial weight lost after 6 months at highest tolerated dose, decide whether to continue, weighing benefits and risks (percentage left out).
